one_line.text: Israeli-American psychologist whose work with Amos Tversky transformed the study of judgment under uncertainty and helped establish behavioural economics.

biography.text: Kahneman was born in Tel Aviv in 1934, studied psychology and mathematics at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, completed a psychology doctorate at the University of California, Berkeley, and later taught at Princeton. He died in 2024. The 2002 economics prize recognised his integration of psychological research into economics, especially judgment and decisions under uncertainty.

background.text: His early research concerned perception, attention and mental effort. A long collaboration with Amos Tversky then produced the heuristics-and-biases programme and prospect theory. Later work examined wellbeing, remembered experience and decision quality. Thinking, Fast and Slow brings those strands into one general-reader account.

expertise.text: Kahneman had direct research expertise in attention, perception, judgment, decision-making and wellbeing. His strongest authority is over the experiments and theories he helped create; the book's broad two-system narrative is an explanatory synthesis rather than a literal map of separate brain machinery.

perspective_and_limits.text: He writes as a reflective experimental psychologist, repeatedly showing how confident intuition can outrun evidence. He is unusually candid about uncertainty and his own errors, but the 2011 synthesis also preserved striking social-psychology findings that later proved fragile. His organising metaphors remain useful only if readers do not mistake them for two literal or exhaustive systems.

selected_works.relationship: The early account of limited attention and mental effort that underlies the effortful-processing side of Thinking, Fast and Slow.

selected_works.title: Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases
selected_works.relationship: The research programme's foundational collection, edited with Paul Slovic and Amos Tversky.

selected_works.title: Choices, Values, and Frames
selected_works.relationship: A collection on risky choice, framing and prospect theory, edited with Amos Tversky.

selected_works.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
selected_works.relationship: The general-reader synthesis of attention, heuristics, risky choice and wellbeing.

selected_works.title: Noise: A Flaw in Human Judgment
selected_works.relationship: With Olivier Sibony and Cass Sunstein, extends the decision-quality project from systematic bias to unwanted variability in judgment.
